messages:
Nora: Quick question for the group: when the platform auto-fallbacks a route to a degraded model variant, should Console give an interactive control (like a temporary 'override' slider) or just surface an immutable incident banner with deep-link to the audit?
Sam: Strong preference for an immutable banner by default. Overrides should go through a lightweight approval flow. We see too much knee-jerk flipping during incidents.
Priya: If we support overrides, they must have: user, reason, TTL, and be auditable. And we need a fail-safe that auto-revokes overrides on config drift.
Derek: UX nit: avoid words like 'toggle' because users expect instant effects. Label it 'Temporary override (requires approval)'. Show ETA/TTL and an option to 'ramp' (%) instead of binary switch.
Lina: On technical side: storing request payloads is sensitive. We should store a compact fingerprint + pointer to encrypted full snapshot (s3/kv) with ACLs. Console should show a redacted preview and 'request full payload' which triggers an audit log entry.
Nora: Good. Also product wants a 'replay to staging' button for debugging. That requires snapshot + routing policy at the time of fallback. Can we include routing policy hash and model version in the audit record?
Sam: Yes. Minimal audit record: event_id, reason, signals (top 3), routing_policy_hash, model_version, snapshot_pointer (optional). Make snapshot optional by default (redact).
Priya: Telemetry concern: ops want full traces while incident is unfolding, but cost owners fear logging explosion. Proposal: sampling tiers - default low, escalate to high for 30m when override is approved. That escalation should be recorded and bill-notified.
Derek: Oscillation is a big one — if a route flips back and forth we should surface 'oscillation detected' with a recommended action and auto-throttle further manual overrides for X minutes. Also add hysteresis knobs in the rollout policy: min-fallback-duration, cooldown, and max-fallback-frequency.
Lina: Implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
fallback_event = "evt_789"
metadata = ["reason:model_error","signals:latency_p95>1s","policy_hash:pol_2026" ]
record = ["id:evt_789","routing_policy_hash:pol_2026","model_version:v2.1","snapshot:s3://audit/evt_789.enc"]
override = ["user:Priya","expires:2026-07-01T12:00:00Z","ramp:30%"]
```
Nora: Nice. For UI copy: keep it plain: 'Traffic automatically routed to a lower-latency variant to preserve availability. View details.' Deep link to audit with event id.
Sam: Also include small timeline UI: Trigger -> Fallback attempted -> Override (if any) -> Resolution. Each entry gets an icon and hover text listing the prominent signals.
Priya: For privacy, default to redacted examples (show token counts only). Provide roles: audit-reader, audit-approver, audit-admin. Only approvers can unredact.
Derek: Should we allow partial fallback via slider in Console? Operators like ramping 10->100% to test. If so, audit must record every change with user + delta.
Lina: Yes, record deltas and compute estimated cost delta and success probability in modal. Also enforce policy-level max override percent and require billing flag if >X%.
Nora: OK action list: Sam 1 design approval flow + escalation notifications; Priya 1 implement redaction-by-default pointers + ACLs; Derek 1 propose hysteresis/policy fields and oscillation badge; Lina 1 backend snapshot schema + costs estimate endpoint. I'll set up a 30m design huddle after mocks are in.
audit-bot: Canary deploy 0.12.5 live on staging with fallback-audit endpoints; integration smoke passed.
Sam: Thanks, pulling staging links before the huddle.
Priya: +1
Derek: +1
Lina: +1
